shortDescription: A dense Mekong Delta river city where a multigenerational household moves through Vietnamese public schools, neighborhood markets, motorbike and bus traffic, river transport and expanding digital life.
longDescription: The World is rooted in Ninh Kiều, Cần Thơ, a major urban center of Vietnam's Mekong Delta. A caregiver, two children and a grandparent share an apartment on a mixed residential-commercial street, with another relative elsewhere in the city. Daily life crosses Vietnamese public schooling, markets, libraries, motorbike and bus routes, river-linked commerce and occasional travel to surrounding delta communities. From 2004 through 2026 the setting changes visibly with urban development and expanding digital access, while waterways, heavy seasonal rain, neighborhood commerce and Vietnamese-language public life remain durable anchors.

visualProfile.overallCharacter: Dense, humid, lived-in Mekong Delta urbanism: ordinary metropolitan Cần Thơ rather than a scenic river postcard.
visualProfile.geographyAndClimate: Low-lying tropical river-city environment in the Mekong Delta, with canals and broad waterways embedded in urban movement, strong sun, humidity and seasonal heavy rain.
visualProfile.builtEnvironment: Mid-rise apartment and mixed-use buildings in Ninh Kiều, Vietnamese public-school facilities, neighborhood market structures, small commercial fronts, a public-library setting, bus corridors and practical river landings.
visualProfile.streetsAndPublicRealm: Motorbikes, pedestrians and buses share active commercial streets; markets spill into the public realm; river access and landing areas are functional parts of transport and commerce; heavy rain can visibly change traffic and street conditions.
visualProfile.interiors: Compact multigenerational apartment rooms, ordinary Vietnamese school classrooms and science/arts spaces, public-library study areas and computers, small shops, food businesses and market stalls.
visualProfile.materialsAndTextures: Painted concrete and masonry, ceramic or practical tiled surfaces, metal shutters and railings, market awnings, wet pavement after rain, river-weathered infrastructure, paper school notices, books, repair materials and everyday commercial goods.
visualProfile.lightAndAtmosphere: Bright tropical daylight, humid haze, reflective river light, deep shade beneath awnings and buildings, darkened storm conditions during heavy rain and warm mixed street/shop lighting after sunset.
visualProfile.vegetationAndLandscape: Urban tropical planting and waterside vegetation may appear around a primarily built metropolitan environment; canals and river edges are ordinary infrastructure, not wilderness.
visualProfile.mobilityAndVehicles: Motorbikes are visually common, alongside walking, city buses and some river transport; private cars should not dominate household mobility.
visualProfile.signageAndLanguage: Vietnamese should dominate ordinary school, civic, shop and market text. English may appear in school material, internet-facing contexts and some tourism-oriented commerce, but should not visually read as a co-primary neighborhood language.
visualProfile.clothingAndEverydayObjects: Contemporary everyday Vietnamese urban clothing across ages; school bags and materials, rain gear when appropriate, motorbike helmets, phones, groceries, books, household repair items and market purchases. Do not use costume or ceremonial clothing as default daily wear.
visualProfile.technologyAndInfrastructure: The chronology moves from more limited early-2000s household/mobile internet access toward widespread smartphones, digital services and newer commercial technology by the 2020s; schools, public computers, motorbikes, buses, utilities and river infrastructure remain visible throughout.
visualProfile.publicInstitutions: Vietnamese public school, Cần Thơ public-library access, city buses, river transport, neighborhood markets and community health services should feel woven into ordinary metropolitan life.

functional river landing connected to ordinary city movement
Vietnamese neighborhood market with groceries, prepared food and repair activity
Cần Thơ library study area with Vietnamese collections and public computers
heavy-rain street conditions without disaster framing

temporalLayers.2004_2010: Fewer smartphones and less pervasive mobile data; internet access is more visibly tied to home computers, schools, public computers or internet businesses; older motorbikes, signage and shop electronics should fit the period.
temporalLayers.2011_2018: Smartphones and social media become increasingly ordinary; commercial streets and public services show visible digital expansion while the same river, market, school and motorbike ecology remains recognizable.
temporalLayers.2019_2026: Smartphones, app-mediated services, QR/digital payment cues where appropriate and newer urban development may appear, without turning Cần Thơ into a generic futuristic Asian megacity.
temporalLayers.continuities: Vietnamese-language public life, tropical rain, Mekong waterways, markets, motorbike-heavy mobility, family apartments, public schooling and river-linked regional movement remain visually continuous.

specific famous landmark substituted for ordinary neighborhood life
luxury skyline as the dominant setting

assetShotIdeas: Hero: ordinary Ninh Kiều mixed-use street with apartments, motorbikes, food commerce and the river-city context visible without becoming a postcard
Mobility: bus corridor and practical river landing during routine school/work travel
Market: neighborhood market combining food, household goods and repair services
Institution: Vietnamese public-school or library scene grounded to the chosen life period
Home: compact multigenerational apartment kitchen/living area
Weather: the same neighborhood during heavy seasonal rain to establish climatic continuity
Time series: one ordinary street corner represented in early childhood, adolescence and 2020s young adulthood
